options.content:
Video sessions grouped into subpopulations, one per city, ISP, CDN and device; each sample is one session's measurement, and larger subpopulations send samples more often. The synthetic data runs 120 minutes with 72 series per metric. | column | what it is | values | |---|---|---| | time | Time of the sample | One sample every 136 ms to 4.29 s, depending on the series | | city | City of the viewer | 6 values: city-0, city-1, city-2, city-3, city-4, city-5 | | isp | Internet service provider of the viewer | 3 values: isp-0, isp-1, isp-2 | | cdn | Content delivery network serving the video | 2 values: cdn-0, cdn-1 | | device | Device type of the viewer | 2 values: mobile, tv | | bitrate | Bitrate level of the session, one of 10 levels | Usual values: Zipf distribution (skew 1) over 10 values
Minutes 70 to 85, ramping in and out over 2 minutes: 50% of samples are random values, uniform over the whole numbers 8 to 10 on the 4 series where city is city-1 and isp is isp-2
Note: whole numbers | | buffering | Rebuffering time of the session, in seconds | Usual values: normal distribution (mean 0.3, standard deviation 0.6)
Minutes 40 to 55, ramping in and out over 2 minutes: 40% of samples are random values, uniform between 5 and 20 on the 6 series where cdn is cdn-1 and city is city-0
Note: never below 0 | | play_time | Play time of the session, in seconds | Usual values: uniform between 55 and 60 | | startup_time | Time until the video starts, in seconds | Usual values: Pareto distribution (alpha 3, scale 1)
Minutes 95 to 110, ramping in and out over 2 minutes: values multiplied by 2 on the 18 series where cdn is cdn-0 and device is tv
Note: never below 0 | | device_id | ID of the viewer's device | Usual values: uniform, upper bound from 42 to 1,317 depending on the series
Note: whole numbers |

Each query runs twice, once with the exact plan and once with the approximate plan. A rule reads query results and decides an action; exact and approx decide separately, and the dashboard compares their decisions. On the time charts below, shaded areas are the problem periods injected into the synthetic data.

**Queries**

| query | PromQL | computed |
|---|---|---|
| entropy_bitrate | `entropy_over_time(bitrate[1m])` | every 60 s over the last 60 s |
| buffering_l1 | `sum_over_time(buffering[1m])` | every 60 s over the last 60 s |
| sessions | `count_over_time(bitrate[1m])` | every 60 s over the last 60 s |
| distinct_devices | `distinct_over_time(device_id[1m])` | every 60 s over the last 60 s |
| startup_p95 | `quantile_over_time(0.95, startup_time[5m])` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |
| rebuffer_ratio | `sum_over_time(buffering[5m]) / (sum_over_time(play_time[5m]) + sum_over_time(buffering[5m]))` | every 60 s over the last 300 s |

**Rules**

| rule | queries it uses | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| hydra | buffering_l1 | Buffering L1 norm above the mean plus 3 standard deviations of the previous 30 minutes (Hydra) |
| hydra_entropy | entropy_bitrate | Bitrate entropy more than 3 standard deviations from the mean of the previous 30 minutes (Hydra) |
| mux | rebuffer_ratio, startup_p95, sessions | Rebuffering above 5% or p95 start time above 4 s over 5 minutes, with at least 100 viewers (Mux) |
| conviva_ai | startup_p95, sessions | p95 start time above the mean plus 3 standard deviations of up to 6 hours, with at least 25 plays; the alert then holds for 1 hour (Conviva AI Alerts) |
| conviva_patent | rebuffer_ratio, distinct_devices | Rebuffering above a baseline decaying by 0.998 per minute plus 3 standard deviations for 5 minutes, with at least 100 devices (Conviva patent) |

panels.title: Every run and query: plan, query error, and what the application saw
panels.description: Each row is one query in one run, paired with one rule or alert that reads it; a query read by three rules has three rows. Sketch and parameters are the approximate plan the planner chose: the sketch type and its size (for KMV, k is how many hashes it keeps; for HLL, precision p means 2^p registers). Fidelity compares the rule's decisions on the exact and approx answers: an episode is a stretch of consecutive evaluations where the exact rule fires, an incident is an attack or change the data generator injected (synthetic data only). Hover a fidelity cell to read all of it.

properties.value: Defined per application. Threshold alert: evaluations where exact and approx agree on firing. Autoscaler: matched scaling actions over matched, false and missed ones. Rollout controller: rollouts decided the same. Top clients: mean clients shared by the exact and approx top lists, as a fraction of the list size. Rule: entity-evaluations where exact and approx agree on whether the rule is active.
